issues.title: Asyncpg with sqlalchemy cannot perform operations at the same time
issues.reason: One execution of the maintainer raw-asyncpg example uses ten Tasks and one real PostgreSQL connection. Nine prepare calls raise the native InterfaceError that another operation is in progress; one returns data. Gather with return_exceptions=True permits bounded cleanup. The connection closes, PostgreSQL logs shutdown and the process exits 0. CoroPerf joins all nine captured exception stacks to their actual Task creation records, recovering the named member-log and moderation submission helpers absent from the native/current exception stacks. An explicitly added API observer records all ten actual Tasks using the same Connection/protocol objects. Together they expose both submission origins and the shared resource; generic Task ancestry alone does not establish connection ownership. This is the maintainer standalone driver component on asyncpg0.29.0, not the original Discord bot or SQLAlchemy1.4 beta ORM. Two named submission helpers and bounded exception collection adapt the example for attribution. Those helper names are fixture entries, not recovered Discord registrations. Two earlier authentication failures are preserved; this is the only successful prepared-statement workload. No per-Task connection fix, alternate version or query replay ran. Known upstream guidance to use distinct connections is not a locally tested fix.

issues.title: server: Set runtime/pprof goroutine labels on server streams
issues.reason: One Go1.23.0/grpc1.60.1 bufconn Health/Check RPC returns SERVING. Its controlled child goroutine171 remains in channel receive during a bounded 30ms snapshot. The native child dump records only enqueueContinuation as immediate creator; the earlier server-handler goroutine170 is absent. Normal child and server cleanup completes with process exit0. Standard runtime trace records goroutine171 birth with the full creator stack through service.Check, the generated gRPC handler and Server.processUnaryRPC. Child self-reported native ID and independent all-goroutine snapshot match the same runtime trace ID. CoroPerf joins birth to the waiting stack and restores the historical gRPC method origin absent from the current stack. The measured trace waiting interval is about 30.96ms. The source information already exists in standard Go trace; CoroPerf supplies the normalized identity join and combined view. This is a controlled diagnostic component illustrating issue9010 on cached Go1.23/grpc1.60.1, not a current Go1.27 regression, the original goroutine-label implementation or a panic/crash reproduction. One in-memory RPC and one child continuation ran. It does not establish a stuck server, resource leak, cross-process request ID or complete RPC causal graph. No modern-label, fixed-version or additional RPC comparison ran.

issues.reason: The relanding tracker includes concrete InfluxDB/Python-plugin evidence: two async workers, default512blocking-thread limit, two rapidly issued HTTP requests and closure-entry logs on one worker. CoroPerf needs actual request→Future→blocking-job→worker associations and enqueue/start/end timestamps plus CPU/wait evidence; ancestry alone cannot prove idle-worker accounting or performance benefit.

issues.title: [serve] Router skips cache invalidation on gRPC request failure
issues.reason: One real grpc.aio request fails with UNAVAILABLE under Ray 2.59.0. Ray receives the same UnaryUnaryCall object in its completion callback, and the queue-length cache entry remains 0 after callback and cleanup. The callback runs with no current asyncio Task; its physical stack omits the original request submission. An explicit observer matches the callback Call to the Call created inside the actual owner Task. Generic asyncio creation, suspended-stack and exit records identify that same Task. CoroPerf joins its recorded creation to the suspended request stack, recovering submit_ingress_request. Four involved Ray source files match their installed distribution RECORD hashes. The callback stack is stored separately and is not mislabeled as owner-Task execution.

issues.title: Logical replication breaks on idle slot since 42.7.11 -> Tried to write to an inactive copy operation
issues.reason: One PgJDBC42.7.13/JDK21.0.1 idle logical-replication read on private PostgreSQL17.1/test_decoding throws PSQLException55000: Tried to write to an inactive copy operation. The status interval is configured to3000ms and the stream reports closed. Target and JDI collector exit0; server shutdown is logged. Source review, artifact preparation, build and execution take166.89s. CoroPerf joins the actual FutureTask constructor object1133 to four later diagnostic observations, recovering startChangefeed absent from the native/current exception stack. An explicit JDI resource observer binds that Task to stream1183 and CopyDual1184, independently checked against application-held Task/stream references. The same operation appears in the SocketTimeoutException, unlock entry, wrapped read failure and subsequent inactive-COPY failure. Seven timeout records are rethrows of one exception object1196, not seven timeouts. The source already documents the root cause; the additional evidence is historical ownership and the same-operation event sequence. The logical output plugin is test_decoding rather than wal2json, within the report explicitly described as plugin-agnostic. A real idle logical stream and unmodified42.7.13 driver are used, not physical replication or a thrown-error stand-in. A single controlled FutureTask supplies the component submission context; startChangefeed is its helper, not an original application registration. Resource identity requires the explicitly added observer and is not inferred from Task ancestry. Event-record order is captured, not physical timestamps; unlock is observed at entry, not exit. No duration, uninstrumented timing, alternate driver/plugin/interval or fix validation is claimed. Only one successful read workload ran.

issues.title: Failed BEGIN leaves Connection._top_xact set; every later transaction becomes a SAVEPOINT and fails with NoActiveSQLTransactionError
issues.reason: One asyncpg0.32.0/CPython3.14.3/private PostgreSQL17.1 run follows the original busy-query example: SELECT pg_sleep(0.5) occupies the Connection, so concurrent BEGIN raises InterfaceError. After the query finishes, the Connection is open and idle but _top_xact still points to that FAILED Transaction. The later transaction sends SAVEPOINT and raises native NoActiveSQLTransactionError, SQLSTATE25P01. Process exit0 and connection/server cleanup succeed. Selection/source/setup/run take115.05s. The actual API-returned busy Task object0x73927aac5a90 independently matches the native pending Task snapshot and generic CoroPerf identity. The selected live sample precedes BEGIN failure; the same Task returns before the later SAVEPOINT error. CoroPerf joins creation2 to pending sample40 and recovers launch_busy_query, absent from the native Task stack and both error tracebacks. Additional API observations bind this Task, Connection0x73927aa75150 and failed Transaction0x73927a86e110 across the two failures. The source already describes stale _top_xact; the added diagnostic fact is the exact busy operation and its historical submission context. This is the original concurrent-query/pre-send BEGIN component, not Aurora/RDS Proxy, SQLAlchemy, a pool or the cancelled-BEGIN variant. Original Task topology is retained: launch_busy_query only names the existing create_task expression, and the later transaction remains inline in main. Resource identity requires the explicit API observer; generic Task ancestry does not infer shared Connection/Transaction ownership. The native pending stack contains execute, and Python continuation inspection stops at the opaque Cython protocol awaiter. One successful scenario; no reset/fix, pool, proxy, cancellation variant, alternate version or additional batch.

issues.reason: Psycopg3.3.6/CPython3.13.5/pure-Python libpq18.7/private PostgreSQL18.7 runs one original timing-sweep batch and stops on its first matching error, at trial2. Trial1 returns CancelledError; trial2 receives2cancel calls but ends with OperationalError: cannot exit pipeline mode while busy. The matching Task has cancelled()false/cancelling()2, and the connection remains in pipeline mode(status1). Native traceback shows cancellation followed by cleanup failure and executemany rethrow. Targetexit0, connections closed, table dropped and private server shutdown. New-batch setup/run79.84s; earlier socket startup failed before any target and is archived. The API-returned Task 0x7b3b4dcf7490 matches CoroPerf generationg3. Creation25 joins cancellation27 and pipeline cleanup OperationalError36, restoring launch_update_batch, absent from native error traceback, completed Task error stack and current.folded. The same Task exits with exception; all14 focused observations are attributed. Explicit API observation26 binds the actual Task/Connection/Cursor within trial2. Connection address 0x7b3b4dd08550 and the underlying coroutine object address were reused between the two trials, while the Task runtime identities remain distinct. The earlier Task is excluded, so address equality is not misread as shared connection ownership. The report already explains cleanup masking cancellation; added diagnostic evidence is the exact operation and its historical submitter at both phases. One upstream batch with2trials, stopped immediately at the first matching error; no400trial distribution, further timing trials, alternative version/implementation or fix comparison. Locally2cancel calls are observed, not the report's exact three-cancellation sequence; exception propagation observations are not distinct exception-object counts. The original victim Task,1000-row table,two UPDATE parameters and delay/gap schedule remain; the helper only names the existing create_task expression. Extra API observations supply resource associations within the matching trial; generic ancestry cannot infer resource ownership, cross-trial object lifetime or cancellation initiator. Harness helper names are not unknown production caller names. Full Chancy worker retry/shutdown behavior is unverified. Report gives PostgreSQL18 without a patch; local18.7 is explicit.

issues.title: AsyncConnectionPool: a cancel that reaches a worker mid-connect is swallowed, so asyncio.run() never returns if the pool was not closed
issues.reason: One reported silent-loopback connect/shutdown scenario with psycopg3.3.9, psycopg-pool3.3.3 and CPython3.12.16 accepts one connection. At0.604s after startup, asyncio.run is still in _cancel_all_tasks; worker0 is unfinished with cancelling()=1 at pool_async.py:679 awaiting q.get. Other pool workers are cancelled. Preparation and the sole run take76.80s. The diagnostic callback saves evidence and exits the process0. The actual Task address0x79ac9a18c100 independently matches asyncio.all_tasks, the pool-held worker reference and the generic CoroPerf creation/sample records. CoroPerf recovers start_connection_pool from the worker creation stack, absent from its later native/current wait stack and unavailable in native debug creation traces. The same worker has a scoped CancelledError observation in _connect/_add_connection before returning to queue wait. The focused capture has30 attributed observations; the catalogue highlights one cancellation observation and the last wait snapshot. The source report already describes cancellation swallowing; the added fact is historical application ownership. This proves a bounded shutdown stall, not infinite duration. asyncio.run does not return normally: the observer calls os._exit(0), closing owned loopback sockets. No pool.close workaround, fix, extra cancellation, reset path, other version or replay was tested. start_connection_pool is a submission helper introduced in this standalone harness. No exception-object identity was captured, so propagation records are not counted as distinct errors. A file-scoped exception probe supplements generic Task birth/sample capture; the original graph is preserved and the focused graph selects only the independently identified worker, without synthesizing runtime events.

issues.title: A queued MP prefetch can wait for the 500 ms poll timeout after its reader finishes
issues.reason: One real CPU StorageManager batch at pinned source50a845b uses1MiB L1, the default0.5 retained-byte watermark and an attached native filesystem L2. An initial request and eight queued requests share eight64KiB resident chunks. After each read release, locked bytes are0 and the next queued request is admissible; its containing actual poll still returns after about500ms with no ready event. Median release-to-result is501.624ms. All nine native completions report8 L1/0 L2 hits. Process and storage/tempdir cleanup succeed;137.85s first check. The final CoroPerf graph is empty, so historical caller recovery is unverified and the selected catalogue stays134. An independent standard-library subprocess regression confirms that a later-exiting helper inheriting the same output can overwrite the parent graph. The collector now isolates helper outputs by PID; eight CLI tests pass. The historical empty file did not record its writer PID, so its exact writer is not proven. No LMCache replay was used to refill capture data.

issues.title: Cancelled transaction entry leaves stale state and a later transaction silently uncommitted
issues.reason: One real transaction-entry cancellation at affected client checkout99356800 leaves the reused Connection at transaction depth1/INTRANS. A later transaction context exits normally, but the same Connection sees1 inserted row and an independent Connection sees0. Explicit rollback raises ProgrammingError. The successful process exits0 and connections/table/private PostgreSQL are cleaned up. Later-batch startup through success takes28.79s; one preceding observer failure in that batch occurred before cancellation. Generic CoroPerf Task creation plus a file-scoped cancellation exception observation restores launch_interrupted_entry. An API-boundary observation after the later transaction exits restores launch_reuse_check. Both helpers are absent from current observation stacks and present in the causal stacks. An explicit Connection/Task observer independently binds the cancelled-entry Task, later reuse Task and rollback failure to the same actual Connection, showing depth1/INTRANS across phases. The two selected joins are3→5 and29→31. A later cleanup Task reuses the reuse Task address, but its distinct runtime generation prevents joining their records. This tests exact checkout99356800e90aa0e7b604f652d714ef0f33422b47 using cached CPython3.14.3/PostgreSQL17.1/pure-Python libpq, whereas the report used3.14.8/18.4. The checkout reads version3.3.9 from installed distribution metadata; this is not a released3.3.9 behavior claim. Connection and context-manager wrapper identities require the explicit API observer; generic Task ancestry does not infer shared resources or hidden AsyncTransaction identity. Submission helpers are introduced for this standalone harness. The source already describes stack cleanup; the added diagnostic facts are historical callers and observed cross-phase resource state. Two earlier observer failures are retained, one in b14 and one in b15; neither reached cancellation. No successful scenario replay, nested-savepoint test, alternate server/implementation/version or fix run. The later reuse block runs in a separate Task for this controlled attribution component; the original report runs that block inline in main. No original production Task topology is claimed.

issues.title: AsyncConnectionPool.check() swallows task cancellation and drops a healthy connection unclosed
issues.reason: One run of the original async pool check/cancel example at exact development source e1fc504e34d13e577730afb19b31388e58f42669 confirms cancellation is swallowed: the check Task returns normally, cancelled() is false, cancelling() is 1, and connections_lost becomes 1. The actual dropped Connection is open, absent from the pool, and still answers SELECT 1 after pool close. CPython3.12.16/private PostgreSQL17.1/pure-Python libpq; exit0, explicit connection/server cleanup, full preparation/run70.30s. The independently held check Task object 0x71894b567040 matches CoroPerf runtime generation g6. Native get_stack contains only check. CoroPerf joins creation11 to the CancelledError observation104 inside pool_async.check and recovers launch_pool_check, missing from both the native pending stack and the cancellation observation. The same Task later exits by return. Extra API observation12 identifies Pool 0x71894b9e8110 and checked Connection 0x71894c0c7c20. Sixty focused observations are attributed; cleanup Tasks reusing the address as generations g7/g8 are excluded. The report already describes the cause; added evidence identifies the actual operation and historical submission context. Read-only diagnostic references retain checked Connections and defer GC: this proves the pool drops an open healthy connection, not durable leakage without the observer. Original min_size3, slow-check sleep0.2s, cancellation at0.1s and existing create_task topology are retained; launch_pool_check only names the existing submission expression. Generic Task ancestry does not infer resource ownership or the cancellation initiator; Pool/Connection identity comes from extra API observations. Exact development source is tested, not cached distribution version metadata. Two exception propagation observations do not prove two exception objects. One successful async component; no replay, sync pool, escaping BaseException, wait_for deadline, starvation, version matrix or fix test.

mysql--bugs--112137.reason: The official report already provides the parallel-reader wait stack, controlled I/O-thread comparisons and a documented synchronous-read repair for MySQL 8.0.37/8.4.0. This report has not established a missing originating caller or task-attribution fact for CoroPerf to recover. No local benchmark or patch was executed.
mysql--bugs--112137.reason_zh: 官方报告已提供并行读取等待栈、I/O 线程数对照，以及 8.0.37/8.4.0 改为同步读取的修复说明。该报告尚未证明存在需 coroPerf 恢复的发起调用者或任务归属信息；未在本地执行基准或补丁。

postgres--mail--da0b1ad82f4faec1b3448678.reason: This specific mail says the async_mode flag placement has no observable effect without timer instrumentation and discusses already-pushed instrumentation changes. It does not establish a reproducible missing-caller problem for CoroPerf. No reproduction was attempted.
postgres--mail--da0b1ad82f4faec1b3448678.reason_zh: 这封邮件指出，未启用计时观测时 async_mode 标记的位置没有可见影响，并讨论已推送的观测代码改动。它本身未证明存在可由 coroPerf 解决的可复现调用者缺失问题；未尝试复现。

apache--flink--flink-41427.reason: The report provides a fully synchronous part-upload call chain and shows that the concurrency setting is never consumed. No missing coroutine caller is established by this report. Read-only review; no S3 workload or patch executed.

apache--flink--flink-41417.reason: The report identifies an unconditional false return in the TTL iterator wrapper. The reported result mismatch does not establish a missing asynchronous caller or task attribution. No reproduction attempted.

apache--flink--flink-6115.reason: A bounded stock-only Flink 1.4.0 MiniCluster check reproduces both branch serialization errors and a healthy control. The exceptions have framework-only serialization frames, but native failed-task logs and execution plans expose the matching branch source line. No added CoroPerf diagnostic fact is established. The reported 1.2.0 workload was not executed.
apache--flink--flink-6115.reason_zh: 有界的原生 Flink 1.4.0 MiniCluster 检查复现了两条分支的序列化异常，并完成健康对照。异常序列化帧虽仅含框架代码，原生失败任务日志和执行计划已显示对应分支的源码行号；尚未证明 coroPerf 增加了诊断信息。未执行报告中的 1.2.0 工作负载。

psycopg--psycopg--1468.reason: The report and merged PR isolate excess writable-socket event-loop round trips. They do not establish a missing caller or task-attribution fact for CoroPerf to recover. This exclusion is a read-only applicability decision, not a local performance or repair validation.
psycopg--psycopg--1468.reason_zh: 报告及已合并 PR 已定位可写套接字上多余的事件循环往返；尚未证明存在可由 coroPerf 恢复的调用者或任务归属信息。此次为只读适用性判定，未在本地验证性能或修复。

ray-project--ray--68086.reason: The report identifies a returned-value classification and callback-contract mismatch: Exception values are mistaken for task failures, and callbacks receive an internal wrapper. No missing-caller evidence is supplied. Ray also documents optional task/actor creation-stack capture, which must be compared before claiming a caller gap. No local Ray workload or patch was executed.
ray-project--ray--68086.reason_zh: 报告指向返回值分类及回调契约差异：Exception 值被误当作任务失败，回调收到内部包装对象；尚无调用者缺失的证据。Ray 还提供可选的任务/actor 创建栈采集，声称存在调用者缺口前须做对照。本地未执行 Ray 工作负载或补丁。

psycopg--psycopg--340.reason: Two released pure-Python drivers and two canonical batches verify 32 historical reader attributions. The same unreleased lock links current waits to acquisition and Task creation after the original reader is collected. Four bounded mechanism controls are distinct from the generator-handoff extension. Explicit generator close is an application cleanup control, not a driver repair.
psycopg--psycopg--340.reason_zh: 两个纯 Python 驱动发布版、两个规范批次共核对 32 个历史读取入口。原读取 Task 回收后，同一未释放的锁把当前等待接回取锁和创建记录。四个有界机制对照与生成器移交扩展分开；显式关闭生成器是应用清理对照，不声称修复驱动。
